title: Pitches that highlight owning assets or a lack of rental obligations accelerate funding for both men and women.
Pitches that reference specific financial institutions or brands tend to fund more slowly for both men and women.
Female borrowers who mention a specific geographical location may fund faster.
Male borrowers who explicitly mention operational risks, such as power cuts or fires, may fund faster than those describing routine activities.
Female borrowers who use phrases emphasizing hard work, such as 'working tirelessly', may fund faster.
Male borrowers who list specific products being sold may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include descriptive information about their geographic location or region may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who describe local geography and tourism of their city may fund faster.
Female borrowers who use generic business labels, such as 'sari-sari store', may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the specific goal of saving money to expand may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their general family structure fund faster.
Female borrowers who include specific demographic details fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a history of previous loan repayments fund faster.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
